studies.Reference: The Association of Kidney Function and Inflammatory Biomarkers with Epithelial Ovarian Cancer Risk.
studies.Authors: Hathaway CA, Townsend MK, Sklar EM, Thomas-Purcell KB, Terry KL, Trabert B, Tworoger SS
studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: In prospectively collected samples, we evaluated the association of kidney function markers and C-reactive protein (CRP) with ovarian cancer risk in the UK Biobank. We used multivariable-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models to evaluate quartiles of serum and urine markers with ovarian cancer risk overall and by histology.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Among 232,908 women (1,110 ovarian cancer cases diagnosed from 2006-2020)
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Potassium was associated with endometrioid (Q4 vs. Q1: 0.33, 0.11-0.98)
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Potassium was associated with endometrioid (Q4 vs. Q1: 0.33, 0.11-0.98) - protective association for endometrioid tumors
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: Potassium was associated with endometrioid (Q4 vs. Q1: 0.33, 0.11-0.98)
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: ovarian cancer cases diagnosed from 2006-2020, evaluated overall and by histology including endometrioid and clear cell tumors
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: quartiles of serum and urine markers including potassium, evaluated in prospectively collected samples
